title: Any tips on optimising token usage across Codex and Claude?
author: No_Degree_8837
selftext:
I’ve been developing games with AI for a few years now, I started back in 2022 copy pasting ChatGPT to VS Code! Mostly just for fun and experimenting. More recently (this past year) I’ve focused on one game idea and really put my head into it. It’s been great so far.

However, I’ve noticed recently that I’m burning through my usage much much quicker than I was maybe a month or so ago - and I’m wondering if it’s something fixable?

It could be just down to a much larger codebase, poor prompting ect, but I’m wondering if anyone has any tips?

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body:
The providers keep messing with the useage limits, however, optimization is always a good idea. 

The best thing IMO is to have a modular architecture, work on each slice seperatly, avoid running long-context tasks and seperate them into smaller tasks instead, higher context is billed at a higher rate.

Reasoning levels matter, throwing lower reasoning at a task that is complex would net you with more tokens used to complete it, while higher reasoning for tasks that don't justify it would be practically wasting tokens. This is sadly not something that can be generalized as in use X reason for Y task, you'd have to figure this bit out based on your experience with the models.

Ask your agent for optimization tips, it has a better undeerstanding of your workflow than us random redditors.

Hope that helps.

replies.author: No_Degree_8837
replies.body:
Thanks, yeah I think I need to take a break from implementation and tweaking and use some tokens on optimising my workflow. Thanks for the reply!

I did have a suspicion that usage limits had been meddled with too
